title: Senseye vs Augury: Predictive Maintenance 2027
summary: Siemens Senseye vs Augury compared: data sources, sensors, who reviews alerts, CMMS integration and pricing, and why Tractian is a stronger choice.
body_markdown:
## Key Points


- Siemens Senseye analyzes data a plant already collects, while Augury installs its own sensors on each monitored machine.
- Senseye coverage stops where a plant has no historian tag or sensor on an asset.
- Tractian makes a stronger choice than both, since its own sensors and AI fault diagnosis feed findings into the CMMS a plant already runs.


Siemens Senseye vs Augury is a choice between two starting points for predictive maintenance. Senseye is Siemens software that forecasts machine failure from historians, IoT platforms and databases a plant already runs. Augury brings its own wireless sensors and sells machine health as a subscription with AI diagnostics and vibration analysts.


That split decides how much of the plant is covered on the first day. This comparison weighs data source, diagnosis, deployment, integration and pricing, then makes the case for Tractian over both.

Senseye is software that reads existing data sources, and Augury is a subscription built around sensors it installs.

## Siemens Senseye: Predictive Maintenance Software on Existing Data


Best for: Plants that already send machine condition data to a historian or IoT platform and want software to forecast failures from it.


Siemens Senseye is cloud-based predictive maintenance software that forecasts machine failure and ranks risks using data the plant already gathers. Siemens offers it as Senseye Cloud Application and as Senseye Predictive Maintenance, a wider package that can include software, services and expert guidance.


### Key features


- **Data sources:** connects to historians, IoT platforms and databases and reads condition and operating data from old and new equipment alike. Sensors can be added, though they are not required to start.
- **Forecasts:** AI models machine and maintainer behavior to flag risks, remaining useful life and priorities across a plant.
- **Shared knowledge:** failure patterns, machine behavior and maintenance insights sit in one platform that teams at several sites can open.
- **Human input:** Siemens describes the analysis as AI combined with human expertise and provides advisory, implementation and optimization support.
- **Rollout:** teams can begin with priority assets and add machines and sites over time.


### Where Senseye fits


Senseye fits a plant whose critical machines already feed condition data into a historian, database or IoT platform. Coverage follows that instrumentation, so a cooling tower fan or transfer pump with no sensor and no stored tag stays outside the forecasts until a data source is added. Learn more about[Siemens Senseye alternatives](https://tractian.com/en/blog/siemens-senseye-alternatives) .


### How much does Senseye cost?


Siemens sells Senseye through its sales team, and its product pages list no price.


### Questions to ask Siemens before you buy


- Which of our critical assets have no historian tag or sensor today, and who supplies the hardware to cover them?
- How many weeks of connected data does a new asset need before its first forecast?
- Who confirms a forecast before a planner acts on it: our engineers or Siemens experts?
- Which parts of the quote are software, and which are services or connectivity work?
- How does a Senseye finding turn into a work order in our CMMS?


## Augury: Proprietary Sensors with Subscriptions


**Best for:** Plants that want Augury sensors, AI diagnostics and analyst review in one subscription.


Augury's machine health service is a subscription with Augury proprietary industrial sensors built in. Its AI detects issues, explains what caused them and prescribes a course of action, and vibration analysts review that guidance.


### Key features


- **Standard sensor:** the Halo sensor reads triaxial vibration, temperature and magnetic flux, with IP66/68/69 protection for wet areas.
- **Slow machines:** an ultrasonic model covers large gearboxes, rotary drums and kilns turning as slow as 1 RPM.
- **CMMS and EAM:** fault details, severity and recommended actions flow into the maintenance system, with named connections to SAP, IBM Maximo, MaintainX, Infor, Limble and Rockwell.


### Where Augury fits


Augury fits a plant with few sensors on its rotating equipment that wants hardware, diagnosis and review from one supplier. Each monitored machine carries Augury hardware, and that hardware is part of the subscription. Learn more about[Augury alternatives](https://tractian.com/en/blog/augury-alternatives) .


### How much does Augury cost?


Augury quotes prices after a demo with its sales team.


### Questions to ask Augury before you buy


- Will the[third-party IoT sensors already on our machines](https://www.g2.com/products/augury/reviews/augury-review-13769996) feed the platform, or do those points need Augury hardware too?
- How much time and effort do[initial setup and sensor integration](https://www.g2.com/products/augury/reviews/augury-review-13784555) take, and how much of that work lands on our team?
- Which[custom reports and direct exports to our other software](https://www.g2.com/products/augury/reviews/augury-review-13715807) exist today, and which are still missing?
- Which alerts does an analyst read before they reach our team, and which arrive straight from the AI?
- Who keeps the installed hardware when the subscription term is over?


## Senseye or Augury: Which Fits Your Plant?


Senseye suits plants that already collect condition data, and Augury suits plants that need sensors installed before monitoring can begin.


Plant situation What to look for Siemens Senseye Augury

Few sensors on rotating assets Hardware that arrives with the analytics Sensors are optional, so those assets need a data source first Halo sensors supplied by Augury


IT owns a Siemens automation stack Fit with the automation and IT systems in place Siemens product, with Industrial Connectivity Services for older machines Listed connections include Rockwell, SAP and IBM Maximo


No vibration analyst on staff A diagnosis a technician can act on without reading spectra AI with human expertise, plus Siemens advisory support Prescriptive guidance backed by vibration analysts


Classified areas Sensors certified for the zone where they sit Set by whichever sensors supply the data A separate hazardous-area sensor family


Test either option on assets whose last failure you documented, for example a process pump that went through two bearing sets last year or the gearbox on a conveyor head drive. Record how many days of warning each system gives and what the alert tells the technician to inspect.


## Tractian: A Stronger Choice Than Senseye or Augury


Tractian is the better pick over both because it covers the path from sensor reading to repair decision in one platform built for condition monitoring and AI asset health. Its Smart Trac Ultra sensors put condition data on machines with no sensor today, its AI tells the team what has gone wrong, the reason behind it and the next move, and findings flow into the CMMS and ERP the plant already runs. Most customers are fully operational within 14 days.


### How Tractian detects and diagnoses faults


A[Smart Trac Ultra](https://tractian.com/en/solutions/ultrasonic-sensor) mounts on one critical machine and records vibration, ultrasound, temperature and RPM from it, sampling at up to 64 kHz.[Auto Diagnosis](https://tractian.com/en/resources/videos/auto-diagnosis) pins those readings on specific faults, for example bearing wear, misalignment or unbalance, and checks each call against bearing libraries and millions of machine hours of history.


Alerts carry a priority based on failure severity and asset criticality, along with the probable root cause and the steps to take. For a second look on a hard call,[supervised analysis](https://tractian.com/en/solutions/failure-detection) adds expert-vetted human review. This sensor-led route to[predictive maintenance](https://tractian.com/en/solutions/predictive-maintenance) means coverage does not wait for a historian tag.


[Energy Trac](https://tractian.com/en/solutions/energy-trac) sits in the electrical panel feeding a motor and tracks current, voltage and power factor. It flags rotor, stator, winding and insulation faults, plus voltage imbalance. Paired with a Smart Trac Ultra on the driven machine, it forms[multimodal monitoring](https://tractian.com/en/solutions/multimodal) , and Janus, the industrial AI Tractian trains on proprietary data from real machines, correlates the mechanical and electrical signals into one diagnosis.


### Implementation, reporting and integrations


- Installation: each sensor is glued or drilled-and-tapped in place and goes live in minutes. Battery life runs up to 5 years.
- **Connectivity:** each sensor sends its readings to a receiver, and the receiver forwards them over 4G/LTE, so the sensors do not depend on plant Wi-Fi, cabling or an IT project.
- **Time to diagnostics:** full operation typically comes within 14 days for most customers, the period the models need to learn each machine's normal behavior.
- **Hazardous and washdown areas:** the IP69K sensor is[Class I Div 1 ATEX/IECEx/NFPA compliant](https://tractian.com/en/solutions/sensor-specifications) .
- **Reporting:** Power BI and SQL connectors, plus links to Looker, Tableau and Excel, let teams shape their own reports on downtime, failure trends and costs.
- **Integrations:**[Tractian integrations](https://tractian.com/en/solutions/integrations) pass findings to MaintainX, Fiix, UpKeep, Limble and other CMMS platforms, plus ERPs including SAP and Oracle NetSuite, while an API reaches SCADA and APM systems.


### Customer results


At plastics manufacturer[Alentra](https://tractian.com/en/case-studies/alentra) , a PFMEA put long-lead-time motors at the top of the risk list, since motors on pharmaceutical jobs could take six weeks to replace. Tractian now gives the team 24/7 visibility across its most critical motors, pumps and compressors, and produced its first confirmed root-cause diagnosis on a motor failure that kept coming back.


Appliance maker[Whirlpool](https://tractian.com/en/case-studies/whirlpool) brought 95% of its previously unmonitored vibration points under coverage and posted an 85% insight validation rate. The plant counts $1M+ in avoided costs from early interventions, prompted by Tractian insights, that headed off downtime and production losses.


### How much does Tractian cost?


Tractian builds each quote around the machines a plant cannot afford to lose. A specialist maps how those assets fail and which signals catch the failure earliest, confirms conditions on site, then prepares a custom quote and coverage plan.[Tractian pricing](https://tractian.com/en/solutions/pricing) starts from that asset list.


## Frequently Asked Questions


### How do Siemens Senseye and Augury differ?


Senseye is Siemens software that forecasts failures from data a plant already stores in historians, IoT platforms and databases. Augury sells a subscription that includes its own sensors, AI diagnostics and analyst support. The choice turns on whether your critical machines already produce usable condition data.


### Does Siemens Senseye need sensors?


Senseye can start without new hardware because it reads existing historians, IoT platforms and databases. Sensors can be added for assets that produce no condition data today. Those assets stay outside the forecasts until a data source exists.


### Is software-only or sensor-based predictive maintenance a better fit for rotating equipment?


Software-only predictive maintenance works where machines already send condition data to a stored source. Sensor-based monitoring adds vibration, ultrasound and temperature readings to motors, pumps, fans and gearboxes that have no sensor yet. Tractian takes the sensor-based route further: Smart Trac Ultra adds RPM to those readings, AI names the likely fault and next step, and findings pass to the CMMS a plant already uses.


### Who should review predictive maintenance alerts?


A reliability engineer or analyst should confirm high-severity calls on critical assets before parts are ordered or a shutdown is booked. Lower-risk alerts can go straight to the planner with the fault name and recommended action. Agree on that split with any vendor before the trial starts.


### Can Tractian sensors be used in hazardous areas?


Yes. Tractian sensors are Class I Div 1 ATEX/IECEx/NFPA compliant and carry an IP69K rating for washdown areas. Tractian sensors reach a receiver that sends the data on over 4G/LTE, so monitoring in classified zones does not depend on plant Wi-Fi.
